name: Jalam
overview: Jalam is a male Edomite figure noted in Scripture as a son of Esau and a chief of Edom. His identity is rooted in his lineage from Esau, the progenitor of the Edomites, marking him as part of the early tribal leadership. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Jalam appears only once in Scripture and no specific meaning or divine origin is attributed to it. It is simply presented as a proper name without further explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Jalam as a son of Esau and Judith, establishing his place within the Edomite family line. Beyond these parental connections, no other family relationships are recorded for him.
scriptureSignificance: Jalam's significance lies in his role as both a son of Esau and a chief among the Edomites, indicating his leadership within this tribe descended from the patriarch Isaac's elder son. His mention underscores the continuation of Esau's lineage and the establishment of Edomite tribal leadership. While brief, his inclusion highlights the biblical record's attention to the genealogical and tribal structures foundational to Israel's neighboring peoples.
